## Authentication

Supports OAuth2 [Authorization Code Flow](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1),
at paths described in the OpenID Connect Discovery metadata document (whose URL is defined by the `OAUTH_METADATA_URL` environment variable).

Microsoft Identity Platform documentation can be read 
([here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow)).

Authentication can be turned off with `OAUTH_ENABLED=false` environment variable. 

When authentication is turned on, all requests to protected API endpoints must provide a valid bearer (JWT) token inside the `Authorization` http header.

- `true` - ascending order

- `false` - descending order

Example: `{"topic_code": true, "name": false}` sorts the returned list by `topic_code ascending`, then by `name descending`.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

schema.description:
Specifies which logical operation - `and` or `or` - should be used in case filtering is done on several fields.

Default: `and` (all fields have to match their filter).

Functionality: `and` will return entities having all filters matching, `or` will return entities with any matches.

parameters.name: total_count

schema.description:
Boolean flag to include the total count of entities in the response.

Default: `false`

Functionality: When set to `true`, returns the total number of entities that match the query.

When combined with filters, the count reflects only the entities matching those filters.

Note: This operation can be expensive for large datasets.

Special case: A value of `-1` indicates that the exact count is unavailable due to performance constraints, but confirms that at least one more entity exists beyond the current page.

post.summary: Create a new version of ODM Study Event
post.description:
State before:
 - uid must exist and the ODM Study Event must be in status Final.

Business logic:
- The ODM Study Event is changed to a draft state.

State after:
 - ODM Study Event changed status to Draft and assigned a new minor version number.
 - Audit trail entry must be made with action of creating a new draft version.

Possible errors:
 - Invalid uid or status not Final.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

post.summary: Creates a new activity instruction template in 'Draft' status or returns the activity instruction template if it already exists.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the activity instruction template
* belongs to a library that allows creating (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.
* The activity instruction template will be linked to a library.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an activity instruction template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an activity instruction is created out of the activity instruction template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The activity instruction template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same activity instruction template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

schema.description: The activity instruction template that shall be created.

201.description: Created - The activity template was successfully created.

400.description:
Forbidden - Reasons include e.g.: 
- The activity instruction template name is not valid.
- The library doesn't allow to create activity instruction templates.

404.description: Not Found - The library with the specified 'library_name' could not be found.

409.description: The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource. This typically occurs when attempting to create or modify a resource that already exists or violates a uniqueness constraint.

This request is only valid if the activity instruction template
* is in 'Draft' status and
* belongs to a library that allows editing (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true). 

If the request succeeds:
* The 'version' property will be increased automatically by +0.1.
* The status will remain in 'Draft'.

Parameters in the 'name' property can only be changed if the activity instruction template has never been approved.
Once the activity instruction template has been approved, only the surrounding text (excluding the parameters) can be changed.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an activity instruction template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an activity instruction is created out of the activity instruction template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The activity instruction template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same activity instruction template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

post.summary: Creates a new footnote template in 'Draft' status or returns the footnote template if it already exists.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the footnote template
* belongs to a library that allows creating (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.
* The footnote template will be linked to a library.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an footnote template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an footnote is created out of the footnote template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The footnote template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same footnote template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

post.summary: Creates a new version of the footnote template identified by 'footnote_template_uid'.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the footnote template
* is in 'Final' or 'Retired' status only (so no latest 'Draft' status exists) and
* belongs to a library that allows editing (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The latest 'Final' or 'Retired' version will remain the same as before.
* The status of the new version will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'version' property of the new version will be automatically set to the version of the latest 'Final' or 'Retired' version increased by +0.1.

Parameters in the 'name' property cannot be changed with this request.
Only the surrounding text (excluding the parameters) can be changed.

post.summary: Validates the content of an footnote template without actually processing it.
post.description:
Be aware that - even if this request is accepted - there is no guarantee that
a following request to e.g. *[POST] /footnote-templates* or *[PATCH] /footnote-templates/{footnote_template_uid}*
with the same content will succeed.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an footnote template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an footnote is created out of the footnote template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The footnote template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same footnote template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

schema.description: The content of the footnote template that shall be validated.

204.description: Accepted. The content is valid and may be submitted in another request.

400.description:
Forbidden. The content is invalid - Reasons include e.g.: 
- The syntax of the 'name' is not valid.
- One of the parameters wasn't found.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

* the specified footnote template is in 'Final' status and
* the specified objective is in 'Final' status and
* the specified library allows creating footnote (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true) and

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.

post.summary: Creates a new criteria template in 'Draft' status or returns the criteria template if it already exists.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the criteria template
* belongs to a library that allows creating (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.
* The criteria template will be linked to a library.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an criteria template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an criteria is created out of the criteria template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The criteria template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same criteria template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

schema.description: The criteria template that shall be created.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

patch.summary: Updates the criteria template identified by 'criteria_template_uid'.
patch.description:
This request is only valid if the criteria template
* is in 'Draft' status and
* belongs to a library that allows editing (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true). 

If the request succeeds:
* The 'version' property will be increased automatically by +0.1.
* The status will remain in 'Draft'.

Parameters in the 'name' property can only be changed if the criteria template has never been approved.
Once the criteria template has been approved, only the surrounding text (excluding the parameters) can be changed.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an criteria template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an criteria is created out of the criteria template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The criteria template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same criteria template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

post.summary: Creates a new criteria in 'Draft' status.
post.description:
This request is only valid if
* the specified criteria template is in 'Final' status and
* the specified objective is in 'Final' status and
* the specified library allows creating criteria (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true) and
* the criteria doesn't yet exist (no criteria with the same content in 'Final' or 'Draft' status).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

post.summary: Creates a new objective template in 'Draft' status or returns the objective template if it already exists.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the objective template
* belongs to a library that allows creating (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.
* The objective template will be linked to a library.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an objective template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an objective is created out of the objective template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The objective template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same objective template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

post.summary: Creates a new endpoint template in 'Draft' status or returns the endpoint template if it already exists.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the endpoint template
* belongs to a library that allows creating (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.
* The endpoint template will be linked to a library.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an endpoint template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an endpoint is created out of the endpoint template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

See the *[GET] /template-parameters/* endpoint for available parameters and their terms.

The endpoint template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same endpoint template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='This is my endpoint for [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

Once the endpoint template has been approved, only the surrounding text (excluding the parameters) can be changed.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an endpoint template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an endpoint is created out of the endpoint template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The endpoint template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

name='This is my endpoint for [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

This request is only valid if the endpoint template
* is in 'Final' or 'Retired' status only (so no latest 'Draft' status exists) and
* belongs to a library that allows editing (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The latest 'Final' or 'Retired' version will remain the same as before.
* The status of the new version will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'version' property of the new version will be automatically set to the version of the latest 'Final' or 'Retired' version increased by +0.1.

Parameters in the 'name' property cannot be changed with this request.
Only the surrounding text (excluding the parameters) can be changed.

**Multiple versions**:

Technically, there can be multiple versions of the activity instruction template with the same version number. This is due to the fact, that the version number remains the same when inactivating or reactivating an activity instruction template (switching between 'Final' and 'Retired' status). 

In that case the latest/newest representation is returned.

This request is only valid if the endpoint template
* is in 'Draft' status and
* belongs to a library that allows editing (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be increased automatically to the next major version.

post.summary: Validates the content of an endpoint template without actually processing it.
post.description:
Be aware that - even if this request is accepted - there is no guarantee that
a following request to e.g. *[POST] /endpoint-templates* or *[PATCH] /endpoint-templates/{endpoint_template_uid}*
with the same content will succeed.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an endpoint template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an endpoint is created out of the endpoint template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

See the *[GET] /template-parameters/* endpoint for available parameters and their terms.

The endpoint template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same endpoint template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='This is my endpoint for [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

schema.description: The content of the endpoint template that shall be validated.

204.description: Accepted. The content is valid and may be submitted in another request.

400.description:
Forbidden. The content is invalid - Reasons include e.g.: 
- The syntax of the 'name' is not valid.
- One of the parameters wasn't found.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`


If any provided search term for a given field name is other than a string type, then equal operator will automatically be applied overriding any provided operator.

post.summary: Creates a new timeframe template in 'Draft' status or returns the timeframe template if it already exists.
post.description:
This request is only valid if the timeframe template
* belongs to a library that allows creating (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

If the request succeeds:
* The status will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
* The 'change_description' property will be set automatically.
* The 'version' property will be set to '0.1'.
* The timeframe template will be linked to a library.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an timeframe template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an timeframe is created out of the timeframe template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The timeframe template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same timeframe template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

- The library doesn't allow to create timeframe templates.

JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.

If the request succeeds:
* The 'version' property will be increased automatically by +0.1.
* The status will remain in 'Draft'.

Parameters in the 'name' property can only be changed if the timeframe template has never been approved.
Once the timeframe template has been approved, only the surrounding text (excluding the parameters) can be changed.

**Parameters in the 'name' property**:

The 'name' of an timeframe template may contain parameters, that can - and usually will - be replaced with concrete values once an timeframe is created out of the timeframe template.

Parameters are referenced by simple strings in square brackets [] that match existing parameters defined in the MDR repository.

The timeframe template will be linked to those parameters defined in the 'name' property.

You may use an arbitrary number of parameters and you may use the same parameter multiple times within the same timeframe template 'name'.

*Example*:

name='MORE TESTING of the superiority in the efficacy of [Intervention] with [Activity] and [Activity] in [Timeframe].'

'Intervention', 'Activity' and 'Timeframe' are parameters.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

the linked `MetaStudyField`, and the graph relationships
(`RELATED_STUDY_FIELD_SELECTION`, `HAS_SEMANTIC_DATA_TYPE`,
`RESPONSE_CODELIST`, `RESPONSE_DICTIONARY`, `VALID_NULL_FLAVOR`) are wired
on the initial save.

JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

patch.summary: Sets trial summary parameter metadata on a CT term name.
patch.description:
Creates a new versioned CTTermNameValue (draft → approve) with the given
TS parameter properties and wires the corresponding graph relationships.

**Scalar properties** stored on the CTTermNameValue node:
`reference`, `required_level`, `cardinality`, `notes`.

**Graph relationships** created from the CTTermNameValue (when the corresponding input field is provided):
- `RELATED_STUDY_FIELD_SELECTION` → `MetaStudyField` (linked via `osb_field_name`; `osb_page_reference` is stored on the MetaStudyField)
- `HAS_SEMANTIC_DATA_TYPE` → `CTTermContext` → `CTTermRoot` on the MetaStudyField (linked via `semantic_data_type_uid`)
- `RESPONSE_CODELIST` → `CTCodelistRoot` (linked via `response_codelist_uid`)
- `RESPONSE_DICTIONARY` → `DictionaryCodelistRoot` (linked via `response_dictionary_uids`)
- `VALID_NULL_FLAVOR` → `CTTermContext` → `CTTermRoot` (linked via `valid_null_flavor_term_uids`)

All existing TS relationships on the value node are replaced on each call.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

State before:

Business logic:
 - If parameter at_specified_date_time is specified then the latest/newest representation of the concept at this point in time is returned. If the timezone is ommitted, UTC�0 is assumed.

 - No change

Possible errors:
 - Invalid uid, at_specified_date_time, status or version.

delete.summary: Inactivate final version of an activity instance (attributes and groupings)
delete.description:
State before:
 - uid must exist.
 - Both attributes and groupings must be in status Final or Retired.
 - At least one of them must be in status Final.

Business logic:
 - Any part currently in Final is moved to Retired (latest Final version kept,
   change_description set, version preserved).
 - Any part already in Retired is left unchanged. This makes the endpoint
   idempotent and lets it recover from a mixed-state instance whose attributes
   and groupings diverged for any reason.

State after:
 - Both attributes and groupings end up in status Retired.
 - Audit trail entries are added only for the part that was transitioned.

Possible errors:
 - Invalid uid.
 - Attributes or groupings are in Draft (not allowed).
 - Both attributes and groupings are already Retired (nothing to do).

post.summary: Batch update groupings for multiple activity instances
post.description:
State before:
 - All specified activity instance UIDs must exist.
 - Each activity instance must belong to a library that allows editing.

Business logic:
 - For each activity instance in the batch:
   1. A new groupings version is created (Draft) if not already in Draft status.
   2. The groupings are updated with the provided data.
   3. The new groupings version is approved (Final).
 - All operations are executed in a single transaction: if any step fails,
   the entire batch is rolled back.

State after:
 - All specified activity instances have their groupings updated and approved.
 - Audit trail entries are created for each version creation, edit, and approval.

Possible errors:
 - One or more activity instance UIDs do not exist.
 - A library does not allow editing.
 - Invalid activity, group, or subgroup UIDs in groupings.

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

post.summary: Creates new compound.
post.description:
State before:
 - The specified library allows creation of concepts (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).
 - The specified CT term uids must exist, and the term names are in a final state.

Business logic:
 - New node is created for the compound with the set properties.
 - relationships to specified control terminology are created (as in the model).
 - The status of the new created version will be automatically set to 'Draft'.
 - The 'version' property of the new version will be automatically set to 0.1.
 - The 'change_description' property will be set automatically to 'Initial version'.

State after:
 - compounds is created in status Draft and assigned an initial minor version number as 0.1.
 - Audit trail entry must be made with action of creating new Draft version.

Possible errors:
 - Invalid library or control terminology uid's specified.

201.description: Created - The compound was successfully created.

400.description:
Forbidden - Reasons include e.g.: 
- The library doesn't exist.
- The library doesn't allow to add new items.

get.summary: Get details on a specific compounds (in a specific version)
get.description:
State before:
 - a compound with uid must exist.

Business logic:
 - If parameter at_specified_date_time is specified then the latest/newest representation of the concept at this point in time is returned. The point in time needs to be specified in ISO 8601 format including the timezone, e.g.: '2020-10-31T16:00:00+02:00' for October 31, 2020 at 4pm in UTC+2 timezone. If the timezone is ommitted, UTC�0 is assumed.
 - If parameter status is specified then the representation of the concept in that status is returned (if existent). This is useful if the concept has a status 'Draft' and a status 'Final'.
 - If parameter version is specified then the latest/newest representation of the concept in that version is returned. Only exact matches are considered. The version is specified in the following format: <major>.<minor> where <major> and <minor> are digits. E.g. '0.1', '0.2', '1.0', ...

State after:
 - No change

Possible errors:
 - Invalid uid, at_specified_date_time, status or version.

patch.summary: Update compound
patch.description:
State before:
 - uid must exist and compound must exist in status draft.
 - The compound must belongs to a library that allows deleting (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

Business logic:
 - If compound exist in status draft then attributes are updated.
 - If links to CT are selected or updated then relationships are made to CTTermRoots.
- If the linked compound is updated, the relationships are updated to point to the compound value node.

State after:
 - attributes are updated for the compound.
 - Audit trail entry must be made with update of attributes.

Possible errors:
 - Invalid uid.

 - uid must exist
 - The concept must be in status Draft in a version less then 1.0 (never been approved).
 - The concept must belongs to a library that allows deleting (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).
 
Business logic:
 - The draft concept is deleted.
 
State after:
 - Compound is successfully deleted.
 
Possible errors:
 - Invalid uid or status not Draft or exist in version 1.0 or above (previously been approved) or not in an editable library.

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`

patch.summary: Update active_substance
patch.description:
State before:
 - uid must exist and active substance must exist in status draft.
 - The active substance must belongs to a library that allows deleting (the 'is_editable' property of the library needs to be true).

Business logic:
 - If active substance exist in status draft then attributes are updated.
 - If links to CT are selected or updated then relationships are made to CTTermRoots.
- If the linked active substance is updated, the relationships are updated to point to the active substance value node.

State after:

parameters.name: filters

schema.description:
JSON dictionary of field names and search strings, with a choice of operators for building complex filtering queries.

Default: `{}` (no filtering).

Functionality: filters the queried entities based on the provided search strings and operators.

Format:
`{"field_name":{"v":["search_str_1", "search_str_1"], "op":"comparison_operator"}, "other_field_name":{...}}`

- `v` specifies the list of values to match against the specified `field_name` field

    - If multiple values are provided in the `v` list, a logical OR filtering operation will be performed using these values.

- `op` specifies the type of string match/comparison operation to perform on the specified `field_name` field. Supported values are:

    - `eq` (default, equals)

    - `ne` (not equals)

    - `co` (string contains)

    - `ge` (greater or equal to)

    - `gt` (greater than)

    - `le` (less or equal to)

    - `lt` (less than)

    - `bw` (between - exactly two values are required)

    - `in` (value in list).


Note that filtering can also be performed on non-string field types. 
For example, this works as filter on a boolean field: `{"is_global_standard": {"v": [false]}}`.


Wildcard filtering is also supported. To do this, provide `*` value for `field_name`, for example: `{"*":{"v":["search_string"]}}`.

Wildcard only supports string search (with implicit `contains` operator) on fields of type string.


Finally, you can filter on items that have an empty value for a field. To achieve this, set the value of `v` list to an empty array - `[]`.


Complex filtering example:

`{"name":{"v": ["Jimbo", "Jumbo"], "op": "co"}, "start_date": {"v": ["2021-04-01T12:00:00+00.000"], "op": "ge"}, "*":{"v": ["wildcard_search"], "op": "co"}}`
